<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919735_theRebbe_388" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919735_theRebbe_388__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There is another interpretation of "shevi" as return from exile, indicating a higher level than those needing redemption, and this distinction is explored.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, there is another interpretation of "shevi,"</t>
    <t s="2">that "shevi" is from the term "return,"</t>
    <t s="3">the return from exile.</t>
    <t s="4">For the term "return"</t>
    <t s="5">[and particularly when it is in conjunction with the word "tifadeh" preceding it]</t>
    <t s="6">indicates that even before the return, he is not in exile,</t>
    <t s="7">but rather he is located in another place</t>
    <t s="8">(the place of exile)</t>
    <t s="9">and needs to go back and return to his place.</t>
    <t s="10">Accordingly, "shevi" are more elevated than those about whom "tifadeh" is said.</t>
    <t s="11">For the term "pidyon" (redemption) applies to one who is in exile,</t>
    <t s="12">(unlike this, where he is merely located in the place of exile)</t>
    <t s="13">and needs to be redeemed from exile.</t>
    <t s="14">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="15">how is it possible that the redemption of those who are in exile is through judgment</t>
    <t s="16">(according to the line of law),</t>
    <t s="17">and the return of those who are merely located in the place of exile</t>
    <t s="18">(who are more elevated)</t>
    <t s="19">is through charity.</t>
    <t s="20">And also it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="21">who are the two types concerning whom "tifadeh" and "shevi" are said.</t>
    <t s="22">For "tifadeh" is said regarding Tzion, which refers</t>
    <t s="23">(as above)</t>
    <t s="24">to Israel who engage in Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="25">and nevertheless they are in exile and need redemption,</t>
    <t s="26">and what is the merit of those called "shevi" who are not in exile.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Exile and captivity apply only to vessels, not to light, as light inherently dispels darkness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And it will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that the matter of exile and captivity applies specifically to vessels,</t>
    <t s="3">because they are in the category of existence of a thing,</t>
    <t s="4">unlike the light,</t>
    <t s="5">which is in the category of nothingness,</t>
    <t s="6">exile does not apply to it.</t>
    <t s="7">And this matter</t>
    <t s="8">(that exile does not apply to light)</t>
    <t s="9">is also understood simply.</t>
    <t s="10">For a little light dispels much darkness,</t>
    <t s="11">meaning that even after the descent and drawing down of light into measurement and limitation</t>
    <t s="12">[for then specifically it is possible to say a little or a lot],</t>
    <t s="13">even then it dispels the darkness,</t>
    <t s="14">to the extent that even a little light dispels much darkness.</t>
    <t s="15">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="16">darkness is automatically dispelled before light.</t>
    <t s="17">[For at the beginning of creation, light and darkness were intermingled,</t>
    <t s="18">but after "God separated between the light and between the darkness,"</t>
    <t s="19">darkness is dispelled before light.]</t>
    <t s="20">And from this it is also understood simply,</t>
    <t s="21">that in light, the matter of exile does not apply,</t>
    <t s="22">for darkness</t>
    <t s="23">(of exile)</t>
    <t s="24">is dispelled before light.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly, the soul is like light and is not in exile, only the body is, yet the soul needs to be returned because it is clothed in the body.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, the same applies to soul and body,</t>
    <t s="1">which are analogous to light and vessel.</t>
    <t s="2">As is known from the statement of my father-in-law, the Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="3">that only the body is in exile, not the soul.</t>
    <t s="4">That is,</t>
    <t s="5">even though the soul is clothed in the body and the body is in exile,</t>
    <t s="6">nevertheless, regarding the soul, this is not a matter of exile.</t>
    <t s="7">But only that because the body is in exile,</t>
    <t s="8">the soul that is clothed in it is located not in its place and needs return.</t>
    <t s="9">And as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="10">"I am asleep in exile, but my heart is awake,"</t>
    <t s="11">that even when "I am asleep in exile,"</t>
    <t s="12">the soul</t>
    <t s="13">(and my heart)</t>
    <t s="14">is awake.</t>
    <t s="15">For since the soul is literally a part of G-d above,</t>
    <t s="16">that even when it is in the manner of "mamash" (actual), from the term "mamashus" (materiality),</t>
    <t s="17">meaning it is clothed in a physical body,</t>
    <t s="18">it is a part of G-d above</t>
    <t s="19">[to the extent that it is literally a part of G-d above],</t>
    <t s="20">and it is known the statement of the Baal Shem Tov,</t>
    <t s="21">that when you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp all of it,</t>
    <t s="22">therefore,</t>
    <t s="23">even after its descent and clothing in the body with the power that separates,</t>
    <t s="24">and even during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="25">it is not in exile, etc.</t>
    <t s="26">And accordingly, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="27">that the term "shevi" refers not only to a special type among Israel,</t>
    <t s="28">but also to the soul of each and every Jew.</t>
    <t s="29">For since the soul is not in exile,</t>
    <t s="30">the term "pidyon" (redemption) does not apply to it.</t>
    <t s="31">But nevertheless, it needs return,</t>
    <t s="32">for since the soul is clothed in the body,</t>
    <t s="33">to the extent that it is affected by the events of the body,</t>
    <t s="34">through the exile of the body,</t>
    <t s="35">the soul is also located in the place of exile,</t>
    <t s="36">and therefore needs return.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
